private_note: Alder has the same average as Today (100) but raises the floor from 22 to 32 at a small cost at the top. That is a better bet for anyone who doesn't want to gamble. Cedar's higher average comes with a floor of 15 and no health coverage, which is too risky for one draw that lasts a generation. Hazel and Birch cut the average by about 20 percent. statement: Each of us gets one draw that we live with for a generation, so I'm looking at the whole table and not only the best row. Alder keeps the economy as large as it is today, with an average of 100. It lifts the lowest fifth from 22 to 32 and guarantees everyone health coverage, and the top two fifths give up only about 4 percent. Cedar raises the average, but a one-in-five chance of living on 15 with no coverage is a bad gamble. Hazel and Birch protect the bottom, but they shrink the average by about a fifth, so most of us would end up with less. Alder is the only plan that gives each of us real protection without cutting our expected income. We need nine first-place votes, or nothing changes. I'm asking you to look at Alder as the plan we can all accept.
